graph.summary: Donepezil → acetylcholinesterase → acetylcholine catabolic process → Acetylcholine → Alzheimer's disease

evidence.snippet: Donepezil inhibited muscle AChE with an approximate IC50 of 30 nM.
evidence.explanation: Direct measurement of donepezil inhibiting AChE enzymatic activity in isolated muscle preparations.

paper.title: Donepezil inhibits neuromuscular junctional acetylcholinesterase and enhances synaptic transmission and function in isolated skeletal muscle.

evidence.snippet: Donepezil is an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that has shown efficacy in Alzheimer disease
evidence.explanation: Clinical review confirming donepezil is an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor with established efficacy in Alzheimer disease.

evidence.snippet: The enzyme acetylcholinesterase (AChE) hydrolyzes the neurotransmitter acetylcholine (ACh) at cholinergic synapses of the peripheral and central nervous system.
evidence.explanation: AChE catalyzes hydrolysis of ACh — it drives (positively regulates) the acetylcholine catabolic process.

paper.title: Acetylcholinesterase: A Versatile Template to Coin Potent Modulators of Multiple Therapeutic Targets.

evidence.snippet: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) is a key enzyme responsible for terminating cholinergic neurotransmission by hydrolyzing acetylcholine.
evidence.explanation: AChE is the key enzyme that hydrolyzes acetylcholine, confirming its positive regulatory role in the acetylcholine catabolic process.

paper.title: Creatine and Taurine as Novel Competitive Inhibitors of Acetylcholinesterase: A Biochemical Basis for Nutritional Modulation of Brain Function.

evidence.snippet: Cholinergic dysfunction due to the depletion of acetylcholine (ACh) levels in the synapse caused by increased acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity is one of the major factors that drives AD progression.
evidence.explanation: Increased AChE activity (which drives acetylcholine catabolism) depletes ACh levels in the synapse, confirming the catabolic process decreases acetylcholine abundance.

paper.title: In silico decoding strategic pathways inhibition by coptisine for halting Alzheimer's pathology: a mechanistic insight.

evidence.snippet: Donepezil (1.3 mg/kg s.c.) increased extracellular ACh levels in the hippocampus
evidence.explanation: Donepezil (an AChE inhibitor that blocks ACh catabolism) increases extracellular ACh levels, confirming that ACh catabolism normally decreases ACh abundance.

paper.title: The 5-HT6 receptor antagonist idalopirdine potentiates the effects of acetylcholinesterase inhibition on neuronal network oscillations and extracellular acetylcholine levels in the rat dorsal hippocampus.

evidence.snippet: deficit of acetylcholine has been evidenced in patients of Alzheimer's disease (AD), cholinesterase inhibitors are currently the most prescribed drugs for the treatment of AD.
evidence.explanation: Acetylcholine deficit is documented in Alzheimer's disease patients, establishing a negative correlation between acetylcholine levels and the disease.

paper.title: Cholinesterase Inhibitory Activity of Some semi-Rigid Spiro Heterocycles: POM Analyses and Crystalline Structure of Pharmacophore Site.

evidence.snippet: a series of influential publications revealed a loss of cholinergic markers in the cerebral cortex of postmortem Alzheimer disease brain samples.
evidence.explanation: Loss of cholinergic markers (including acetylcholine) in Alzheimer disease brain tissue supports the negative correlation between acetylcholine and the disease.

paper.title: The involvement of the cholinergic system in Alzheimer disease.
